title: She grew up in India, studied at Osmania University - and just won Harvard's highest honor for alumni.

sources.text: New India Abroad - Anjana Rao awarded Harvard's 2026 Centennial Medal

caption:
She grew up in India, studied at Osmania University - and just won Harvard's highest honor for alumni.

Born in Washington, DC, Rao grew up in India and earned her bachelor's and master's degrees at Osmania University in Hyderabad, before going to Harvard for her PhD in biophysics in 1978.

Now a professor at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology and UC San Diego, Rao's work on gene activation mechanisms in T cells has shaped modern immunology and epigenetics.

Rao's path - educated in Hyderabad, now honored by Harvard - is one more case of an Indian degree carrying someone to the top of global science.
